steps.text: I'll go ahead and submit as malicious. The fax service entity doesn't exist, so I'll skip that step and note the relevant artifacts: host, user, and processes.

submission.reasoning: On workstation5, user wardog ran an elevated cmd.exe (proc-690e6c933a). At 00:45:33 it ran sc.exe (proc-f4d3576242) to point the Fax service's binPath at powershell.exe -noexit -c "write-host 'T1543.003 Test'". At 00:45:35 it ran 'sc start Fax' (proc-cd222a569d). The service then launched powershell.exe (proc-7f9f3418e9) as NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE, so code ran through the hijacked service. At 00:45:41, 'sc config Fax binPath= C:\WINDOWS\system32\fxssvc.exe' (proc-babd722e6c) set the original path back. This is an Atomic Red Team-style simulation of T1543.003 (modifying a Windows service for persistence or execution). I'm treating it as malicious because the same steps would let an attacker hijack a service. Action: confirm the Fax ImagePath is back to fxssvc.exe, and review the wardog account.
